edits.before: Level 1 is even because neither of you can commit — Alistar lacks his combo and you're just poking and stacking.
edits.after: Level 1 favors Alistar — his Q chips through your pickups and you have no answer to a walk-up trade yet.

edits.before: Level 2 stays a skill matchup since your Q range trades evenly against his emerging W-Q threat.
edits.after: Level 2 favors Alistar — Headbutt-Pulverize both punishes your range and threatens the whole duo.

edits.before: Level 3 remains even as both sides trade cooldowns without a clear engage advantage.
edits.after: Level 3 still favors Alistar — Trample stacks punish any prolonged trade near his minions.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still skill-dependent, hinging on whether you dodge his walk-up W-Q.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay Alistar's — dodging his walk-up W-Q is the only lever, and he keeps forcing it.

edits.before: Dawning Shadow online — the global beam saves dives and finishes recalls.
edits.after: Unbreakable Will makes his all-in near-unkillable — W-Q into R still wins the fight before your global beam matters.

edits.before: First item: the Q chunks and the soul thresholds start mocking trade math.
edits.after: His tanky ult-backed engage still out-threatens your not-yet-online scaling — his first item buys more all-in than yours buys range.

edits.before: Late Senna out-ranges the game from the support slot — souls, beams, and mist.
edits.after: Fully stacked Senna out-ranges Alistar's melee engage entirely — souls, crit, and lifesteal put you out of walk-up range.

edits.before: - Alistar Headbutt: matchup-defining — The headbutt-pulverize combo starts every play — respect flash range while it is up. Read it before every duo step-up. - Your E Curse of the Black Mist answers exactly one disaster per cooldown. - Spend the R on swing moments only.
edits.after: - Headbutt (W): 14s down to 10s, closes the gap into Pulverize's knockup — walk it down, don't step to it. - Your own Last Embrace (W) is 11s — root his engage the instant he closes, not after he lands it. - Keep Dawning Shadow (140s-100s) for the all-in, not the poke.

edits.before: Good trade: Q off a minion through their pair — the cast healed your carry, billed theirs, and grew your range. Bad trade: Walking through an open lane for one soul with a hook champion watching — the curve doesn't pay death benefits.
edits.after: Good trade: root his Headbutt-Pulverize whiff, then all-in while Triumphant Roar isn't charged — deny the stun stacks he needs to reset it. Bad trade: an extended chip fight — Triumphant Roar heals him back, so hold Grievous Wounds before you commit.

edits.before: Q off a minion through their pair — the cast healed your carry, billed theirs, and grew your range.
edits.after: Last Embrace is 11s — punish him with a root the moment he closes, before Pulverize can follow up.

edits.before: Walking through an open lane for one soul with a hook champion watching — the curve doesn't pay death benefits.
edits.after: Piercing Darkness heals you, but his combo out-trades a straight duel — bait Headbutt out empty before you commit, don't answer his all-in with yours.
